A0.reason: Full compute grid on EVERY regime, no bandwidth-knee cap. Per-regime active-core check (interleaved: active == min(grid, total_blocks)): square 64/64, wide-short 64/64 (via the W split — see the w_split knob and test_grid_fill_on_wide_short_shape), multiblock 64/64, smallest 2/2 (= total_blocks). Sharded regimes are not in SUPPORTED yet (see A2/C14).

measured.note: off = single core; 4.12x. Also 4.53x on wide-short (13315 vs 60306) and 4.76x on multiblock (170508 vs 811716). The w_split arm is the per-regime grid-fill proof: on wide-short the OFF arm cannot even be BUILT (the pure height split's input CB is WT=512 tiles -> L1 OOM), pinned by the strict-xfail bench arm.

A1.reason: split_work_to_cores(row_wise=True) is kept (design-binding, costs nothing), but on this interleaved DRAM path the round-robin page->bank mapping makes core placement irrelevant: the delta is inside the 2-3% noise band on every benched regime.

measured.note: 2.4% = noise. wide-short 13315 vs 13364, multiblock 170508 vs 168659 (off marginally faster), smallest 2889 vs 2812.

A2.reason: Refinement 1: the sharded path launches on exactly the cores that hold shards, in shard order (ttnn.get_optimal_worker_cores_for_sharded_tensor), instead of the whole compute grid — a core with no shard would have nothing local to tilize. Pinned structurally by test_local_shard_launches_only_on_cores_that_hold_data (4 shards -> 4 cores). The zero_copy=0 arm is its only counterfactual and CONFLATES A2 with C14 (turning the placement off also restores the generic full-grid block split), so the number below is the pair's, not A2's alone; A2's own contribution on these shapes is the dispatch cost of the idle cores.

measured.note: Conflated with C14 (same knob). Interleaved cells are unaffected: A0 keeps the full grid there. | Refinement 2 REFINES this: launching only on the cores that hold data pays only while those cores still move data in big enough transfers. An aliased destination pins WT_CHUNK to the shard width, and below MIN_STREAM_READ_BYTES (256 B) the shard's few cores LOSE to the full grid — measured 1.66x (128 B reads) and 3.21x (one-tile-wide destination shard, 64 B reads). Hence the new `xfer_gate` knob.

A3.followup: Place each reader adjacent to one DRAM bank and give it its own VC, per tech_reports/Saturating_DRAM_bandwidth. This is the single largest identified headroom: the op measures 63-68% of the 288 GB/s DRAM peak and the tech report's recipe reaches ~92%.
A3.reason: Interleaved round-robin means every reader touches every bank -> maximal route overlap. Needs a bank-aware work split, which is a topology change, not a knob turn.

A4.reason: There is no cliff core to specialize: n_chunks is snapped to an exact divisor of WT, so every block is the same width, and the block-count remainder is absorbed by split_work_to_cores' two groups running the SAME kernel with a different num_blocks runtime arg.

B0.reason: Every per-core-overhead lever is counterfactualed on the SMALLEST regime (d_smallest, [1,1,32,64] = 2 tiles on 2 cores) as well as the large ones. B7's win is 8-14% on the large regimes and inside noise on the smallest — it is not gated because it never REGRESSES there.

measured.note: smallest-regime arm for the B-group levers; 1.8% = noise.

B5.reason: Writes are whole TILE pages (one noc_async_write per page); reads are whole sticks whenever n_chunks == 1 and a contiguous WT_CHUNK*32*elem byte range otherwise. The OFF arm splits each page into two half-page transactions.

measured.note: 2.4% (wide-short 13929 vs 14311 = 2.7%; square and smallest inside noise). Small but never negative, and whole-page writes are the structural precondition for B7's per-block barrier. | Refinement 2 measured the READ side of the same proposition, where the swing is far larger than on the write side: the per-row read is WT_CHUNK*32*elem and an aliased destination shard pins it. xfer_gate=1/0 on [1,1,1024,256]: 19,936 vs 33,126 ns at 128 B reads (1.66x), 16,827 vs 53,945 ns at 64 B reads (3.21x). 256 B is the measured knee (at 256-512 B the local destination still wins 1.19x-2.06x), which is what MIN_STREAM_READ_BYTES encodes.

B6.followup: Sweep WT_CHUNK below its L1 cap so the per-stick read lands at <= 512 B (the WH one-packet fast path) and measure against the current coarsest-chunk choice.
B6.reason: The derivation deliberately maximizes the chunk (B5), which pushes reads ABOVE the one-packet size on most shapes. On wide-short it already lands at exactly 512 B (WT_CHUNK=8, bf16). The two levers pull in opposite directions and only a sweep can price them.

B7.reason: One noc_async_write_barrier per BLOCK (WT_CHUNK pages), not per transaction; the reader's per-block barrier is the library helper's.

measured.note: 14.2% win. square 92859 vs 100553 (8.3%), wide-short 13315 vs 14990 (12.6%), smallest 2889 vs 2942 (noise, no regression).

B8.followup: Custom reader with NT_BLK > 1: reserve NT_BLK*WT_CHUNK pages, tag each block with a trid, issue NT_BLK*TILE_H reads and barrier on the PREVIOUS trid. NT_BLK is already a named knob and the CB formula is already written against it; the blocker is that the library reader barriers once per tile-row.
B8.reason: Only measurable on a >=2 blocks/core shape — the bench has one (c_multiblock, 4 blocks/core), so the lever is visible to the bench and this is a real deferral, not a bench gap.

B9.reason: Reader on ReaderConfigDescriptor (NCRISC/NOC0), writer on WriterConfigDescriptor (BRISC/NOC1). The OFF arm swaps them.

measured.note: 2.63x — the largest single-lever win measured. wide-short 13929 vs 32783 (2.35x), multiblock 173311 vs 357969 (2.07x), smallest noise.

B10.followup: Assign a distinct VC per reader so DRAM responses stop serializing first-come-first-serve; pairs with A3.
B10.reason: Needs the bank-adjacent placement of A3 to be meaningful; measured DRAM utilisation (63-68% of peak) is consistent with response-queue serialization.

B11.reason: Misalignment cannot occur: the read chunk is WT_CHUNK*32*elem and the write is a whole tile page, both structurally multiples of the 32 B DRAM alignment for every supported dtype.

B12.reason: tilize is a pure permutation of byte positions: every input byte belongs to exactly one block on exactly one core under either split axis. There is no reuse-shared operand and no dependent axis, so nothing is ever read by more than one core and there is nothing to fan out.

B13.followup: Writer set_state/with_state: the WT_CHUNK writes per block are same-shape, same-size — the natural fit. Sweep it across transaction size (a prior run found it LOSES at 512 B and WINS at <=128 B, so it must be swept, not argued).
B13.reason: Not built this phase. Visible on d_smallest and c_multiblock, both benched.

C14.reason: Refinement 1: both CBs are placed ON the resident L1 shard via ttnn.cb_descriptor_from_sharded_tensor when the shard spec matches the blocking, so the reader publishes pages it never fetched and the writer drains pages it never sent — zero NoC traffic on a local-shard side. The OFF arm (zero_copy=0) takes the TensorAccessor path over the very shard already resident in L1, which is the 'tolerated, not implemented' sharding this lever replaces. Measured 3.7x on the smallest sharded regime and 9.5x on the 8-blocks/core one, so it pays in BOTH regimes (no work-per-core gate needed).

measured.note: smallest sharded regime, HEIGHT-sharded 4 cores, bf16 -> 3.75x. Larger regime [1,1,2048,256] HEIGHT-sharded 8 cores: 4901 ns on / 46548 ns off -> 9.50x. Ablation on the ON arm: full 4901 -> no_compute 862 -> sync_only 856, i.e. the zero-copy path has NO measurable data movement left and is bound by the tilize LLK. | Refinement 2 adds two measured arms on the same knob: padding into a resident destination shard [1,1,2040,256]->[1,1,2048,256] x8 = 22,466 ns ON vs 30,396 ns OFF (1.35x — per-side eligibility: only the INPUT is disqualified by the fill), and the cross-spec L1 gather [1,1,1024,256] WIDTH x2 -> HEIGHT x8 = 18,487 vs 19,464 ns (1.05x; DM-bound, and with a 2-core source the fan-in is the wall, not the placement).

C15.reason: Refinement 1 accepts L1-sharded input and/or output, so the DRAM leg disappears on the sharded side(s): a same-spec sharded call touches DRAM zero times (both CBs alias their shard) and a crossover keeps only the interleaved side's leg. Same knob as C14 — the zero_copy=0 arm is the only counterfactual that removes the placement, and it also restores the NoC traffic this row is about.

measured.note: Same-spec sharded [1,1,2048,256] bf16 measures 4901 ns (427.9 GB/s of effective read+write) against 46548 ns when the same shard is re-fetched over the NoC; the DRAM->shard crossover of the same shape measures 14768 ns (142 GB/s), i.e. exactly one DRAM leg left. The DRAM floor does NOT describe the zero-copy rows — they are L1/compute bound (see C14's ablation), which is the re-target Refinement 3 must apply. | Refinement 2: still holds when the destination is packed from a PADDED stream (1.35x) and when the source is another core's narrow shard (1.05x).

C16.reason: Depth-2 CBs are kept because the public API mandates use_double_buffer=True as the default and the L1 cost is bounded by the CB budget — but the read/compute/write overlap they buy is not visible at these shapes: the op is DRAM-bandwidth-bound, so the reader cannot run ahead.

measured.note: depth-1 is 2.3% FASTER = inside the noise band. wide-short 13315 vs 13426, multiblock 170508 vs 172103, smallest 2889 vs 3041.

C17.reason: The input is ROW_MAJOR and the output TILE — different byte orderings of the same values, so the op can never alias one buffer onto the other.

D18.followup: Build the OFF arm (runtime-resolved accessor args) and price it.
D18.reason: APPLIED in the kernels: TensorAccessorArgs are appended last as COMPILE-TIME args on both the reader and the writer, so address generation is unrolled per shape. What is deferred is the counterfactual arm, not the lever.

D19.followup: Build the OFF arm (pass geometry as runtime args) and price it against the program-cache hit.
D19.reason: APPLIED: the only runtime args are the two buffer base addresses plus the per-core block range and the pad word; all geometry is compile-time. test_tilize_program_cache pins the cache hit.

D20.reason: The compile-time reader-regime selector (R_ALIGNED vs R_PAD, keyed on the pad region actually being non-empty) IS kept — it is a design contract (§5.1: pad_mode='auto' on an aligned input must not take the pad reader) — but on this DRAM-bound path the pad reader's extra per-row bookkeeping is free: forcing it on the aligned path costs nothing measurable.

measured.note: OFF (pad reader everywhere) is 1.5% faster = noise. wide-short 13929 vs 13450, multiblock 173311 vs 172796, smallest 2843 vs 2970.

D21.followup: Build the OFF arm (per-core indexing computed in-kernel from a global block id) and price it.
D21.reason: APPLIED: the host computes each core's [start_block, start_block+num_blocks) range; the kernel only does the block -> (wc, row) divmod. The counterfactual arm is what is deferred.

E22.followup: Whole-model concern (Metal Trace + multiple command queues + events); revisit when tilize is measured inside a model, not standalone.
E22.reason: Outside a single op's scope. The op-level number measured here is device kernel time, which trace does not change.

F23.reason: The rule F23 protects (never downgrade a precision knob the CALLER supplied) cannot be violated here: tilize exposes no ComputeKernelConfig, so there is no caller-supplied precision knob. The one precision decision the op does make (fp32 DEST) is gated on the dtype PAIR — see F25.

F24.regime: float32 -> bfloat8_b and bfloat16 -> bfloat8_b casts (the only bf8b-emitting cells). bfp8_pack_precise is left at its CHEAP default (False), which is the optimal setting, so nothing expensive is inherited — but the arm was not measured this phase.
F24.reason: bfloat8_b IS in SUPPORTED[output_dtype], so the lever is applicable and cannot be closed structurally. No bf8b bench arm exists yet.

F25.reason: fp32_dest_acc_en (+ UnpackToDestFp32 on the input CB) is enabled ONLY when the datums really are 32-bit on both sides (fp32 -> fp32), which is exactly F25's rule. It is what makes that transition bit-exact rather than tf32-truncated; every other dtype pair leaves DEST cheap.

measured.note: the exactness costs 0.7% here and <=3% on the other regimes (wide-short 27737 vs 26903, multiblock 363494 vs 359438) — i.e. the knob is nearly free where it is needed, and off everywhere else.

F26.reason: A lossless unpack path buys nothing downstream of an FPU phase, and tilize IS one: the tiled output is re-read through SrcA/SrcB by every FPU consumer. The kernel always requests Fp32Mode::Fast.

F27.reason: tilize performs NO arithmetic — the LLK reinterprets byte positions. There is no multiply whose math_fidelity could be lowered, and the compute kernel calls no fidelity-sensitive API.

notes.L4_split_reader: Design lamp L4 (master.md example T2 `split_reader`, ~1.7x) becomes APPLICABLE for the first time with Refinement 1: on a sharded-OUTPUT plan the writer issues no NoC work at all, so BRISC is free to take half the reader's DRAM reads on the interleaved->shard crossover. Not built here (Refinement 1 is placement only); it is Refinement 3's business. It has no Part-2 catalog ID, hence this note rather than a levers row.
notes.phase1_stale_closure_reread: The 10 'possibly unlocked' staleness signals are the topology block moving from interleaved-only to interleaved + three sharded plan paths. Re-read at Refinement 1 and all still hold: A1 (row_wise) is INAPPLICABLE on the sharded path (cores come from shard order, split_work_to_cores is not called); A4 (cliff cores) — derive_shard_blocking makes WT_CHUNK divide shard_wt exactly and uneven shards fall back to the accessor path; B11 — a shard row is shard_w*elem with shard_w % 32 == 0, still a 32 B multiple; B12 — destination tile regions are disjoint, so even the cross-core gather reads no byte twice; C16 — an aliased CB has no depth and the zero-copy path is compute-bound (ablation: 4901 -> 862 with compute stubbed), so there is still nothing to overlap; C17 — RM-in / TILE-out still cannot alias (the two aliased CBs sit on different tensors); D20/F23/F26/F27 are untouched by placement.
notes.R2_xfer_gate: Refinement 2 added the `xfer_gate` knob (LEVERS, default 1) with both arms in _bench_tilize.py (test_bench_lever_xfer_gate, test_bench_lever_xfer_gate_narrow_destination). It decides whether aliasing the DESTINATION shard is worth the read transfer the shard's width pins: 1.66x / 3.21x in favour of the grid split below the 256 B knee, no effect above it (dram->HEIGHT x8, 512 B reads: 7,983 vs 8,058 ns). It never gates a SOURCE-local plan — the writer always moves whole TILE pages, measured 0.94x (2 cores) to 3.85x (8 cores). Mechanism-wise this is B5 (transaction size) crossed with A2 (core placement); it has no catalog ID of its own.
notes.R2_reshard_retarget: Re-target for the reshard rows: with the destination local there is NO write traffic, so the ceiling is the SOURCE shard's L1 egress (2 cores x 256 KB in 256 B transfers ~= 14 GB/s/core), not the DRAM floor. Ablation on [1,1,1024,256] WIDTHx2->HEIGHTx8: full 18,487 -> no_compute 17,615 (-4.7%) -> sync_only 745 ns, i.e. DM-bound (95%). Remaining headroom is the source-side fan-in, which the CALLER picks (shard spec), plus L4 split_reader — now MORE applicable than at Refinement 1, since on a destination-local gather BRISC does no NoC work at all.
notes.phase2_stale_closure_reread: The 10 staleness signals at Refinement 2 are the topology block gaining three plan paths (padded-into-local-shard, the paged cross-spec gather, and that gather on the full grid). Re-read, and all still hold: A1 (row_wise) — still not called on a shard-pinned plan, and the GATED gather does call split_work_to_cores again but over the same round-robin DRAM/L1 page map where it measured as noise; A4 (no cliff width) — derive_shard_blocking still divides the shard width exactly, and Refinement 2's uneven grids split ROWS, not W, so the short last shard is a cliff in H that the per-shard block count absorbs (no second kernel width); B11 (32 B transactions) — now stronger, since every page slice of the gather is a 32 B multiple by construction and the one geometry that would break it is refused (test_unaddressable_shard_row_is_refused); B12 (no mcast/semaphores) — still zero, now asserted per-descriptor in test_reshard_placement_and_source_page_geometry; C16 (double_buffer) and D20 (regime_select) — unchanged on the interleaved rows they were measured on, though both now have a new consumer (the gather streams through the input CB and forces R_PAD), so they are the two rows most worth re-measuring in a perf phase; C17 / F23 / F26 / F27 — the format, precision-knob and arithmetic facts they rest on did not move.
